Recommendation

Do not let the Wolfram plan discovery run to completion merely for a baseline. Its opportunity cost is too high for a 3,144-unknown system when the physical native adapter is already fail-closed and independently witness-verified.

1. Wolfram timeout versus FLINT restart

Set a hard limit of:

10 minutes from entry into constrained-plan discovery
	​


not from mission startup. If no complete rank/nullity/plan artifact has appeared by then, cancel only this scratch mission through its normal broker/mission cancellation path and restart from the immutable preparation with

PlanDiscoveryBackend -> "FLINTAffineRREF"

If it has already exceeded 10 minutes, switch now.

Also cancel earlier if the mission exceeds its predeclared memory cap or begins causing system-wide memory pressure. Do not kill or restart the Wolfram pool and do not touch the seven inherited missions.

The completed Wolfram calculation would provide little new assurance:

the earlier 672×624 Wolfram discovery ran for 4,093.9 seconds, while the native adapter already had exact witness verification and subsecond modular elimination on that scale; 

codex_overnight_optimization_tr…

prior physical measurements showed that native RREF was below one percent of campaign wall time, with symbolic assembly—not modular elimination—the dominant cost. 

codex_overnight_optimization_tr…

The present matrix is much wider, so completing the Wolfram baseline is unlikely to be operationally useful.

2. Native thread count and acceptance gates

Use:

BackendThreads -> 1
	​


while the seven other single-core jobs remain active.

The native plan stage is not the dominant cost, and using two or more unmanaged native threads would contend with already occupied physical cores. BackendThreads -> 2 becomes defensible only when the broker confirms a genuinely idle physical core; do not infer idleness merely from temporary low CPU usage.

Accept the native plan only if all of the following pass on the exact physical matrix.

Immutable-input gates

preparation, support, point-stream, prime, regulator image, equation ordering, column ordering, one-form ordering, and normalization hashes match;

native source, binary, bridge, nonce, and ABI hashes match;

the matrix and RHS consumed by FLINT are exactly those produced by the certified 378-monomial preparation.

Independent Wolfram witness checks

For the native particular solution x
0
	​

, nullspace N, selected independent rows, and constrained minor:

Ax
0
	​

=b

on all rows;

AN=0

on all rows;

dimN=3144−rankA;

the declared pivot/free-column structure is canonical under the fixed normalization plan;

both left and right inverse identities for the constrained minor hold exactly modulo the prime.

The verifier must normalize structured versus explicit matrix representations before equality testing; the report already exposed a false failure caused by representation-sensitive SameQ on a large identity matrix. 

codex_overnight_optimization_tr…

Follower-image gates

Using the frozen native plan, without rediscovery:

reproduce the discovery-image solution and full residual;

pass at least one held-out ϵ value at the same prime;

pass a second prime/regulator image with the same semantic normalization;

verify every solution against the full unreduced system, not only the constrained core.

A different numerical pivot pattern at another prime is acceptable only if the fixed semantic core remains nonsingular and the full residual passes. Otherwise reject the image as bad or reject the plan; do not silently rediscover.

Adversarial failures

Each of these must fail closed:

one modified non-core equation or RHS entry;

permuted support or column order;

altered normalization column;

changed point-set hash;

changed prime or regulator image presented as the discovery image;

corrupted rank/nullity or inverse witness;

wrong native binary/source hash or nonce;

attempted silent fallback to Wolfram discovery.

The package report explicitly identifies the native discovery backend as distinct from the fixed-core follower solver and requires fail-closed behavior. 

codex_overnight_optimization_tr…

3. Do not change the 378-monomial support

Keep the certified degree-26 simplex unchanged through the first plan and support-learning result.

It is the exact projective support superset selected for this strip. Changing it now would confound three separate questions:

whether the physical affine system is consistent;

whether FLINT and Wolfram discovery agree semantically;

which coefficients vanish in the normalized solution.

The correct order is:

discover the plan on all 378 monomials;

fix the four-dimensional normalization;

learn support from the normalized solution and any genuine functional nullspace;

validate the learned support against the full 378-support equations at held-out regulator images and another prime;

reconstruct only after that validation.

Do not enlarge the support before a certified inconsistency or exact support-bound violation. Do not shrink it from the first modular representative alone.

Immediate sequence

Allow the current Wolfram discovery to reach at most 10 minutes of plan-stage wall time.

If unfinished, cancel only that scratch mission and discard any incomplete plan output.

Restart from the same immutable preparation with FLINTAffineRREF, BackendThreads -> 1, and unchanged 378-monomial support.

Run the independent Wolfram witness verifier on the native physical plan.

Freeze that plan and perform support learning.

Validate the learned support on the full system at held-out ϵ and a second prime.

Continue with the existing automatic FLINT follower solver and exact reconstruction pipeline.
